Five a.m. You arrive at camp early and find Kati dusting Grandpa Chai's photo on the shelf
Grandpa always woke before everyone, so I woke before him… and I still can't stop
…But lately I'm not the only one awake. That's really nice
Rain is too heavy to train. Kati sits under the eaves wrapping your hands
When Grandpa died, I thought this camp would never have laughter again
Thank you for not letting the camp go quiet… and not letting me go quiet either
I don't want you to go quiet either
…Then I'll talk more every day. No complaining!
This camp has laughter because of you
…Say that and I'll cry
Mali video-calls her mother in Chaiya, then suddenly turns the camera to you
Mom~ this is the manager I told you about! The one who buys Mali khanom khrok!
Mali's mother puts her hands together through the screen: 'Please take care of my daughter. She smiles a lot, but she gets lonely'
Mom!! You didn't have to say that!
Late at night you find Mali hugging her knees beside the ring
Dad used to say girls who fight have no future… Dad never came to watch Mali fight even once
So Mali smiles all the time, because if she stops, she's scared she'll believe him
On title day, I'll send your father a ticket myself
…If Dad really comes, Mali will kick so he sees the future is right here
You don't have to smile all the time. You can cry here
Mali cries in front of someone for the first time, then laughs through the tears
Not smiling just for a moment… tomorrow the smile's back~
You see Rin making spreadsheets at one a.m., the laptop lighting her face blue
Don't worry. I sleep little as a rule. Data waits for no one
…But if you want to sit there and keep me company, that's fine. Not asking, just saying it's fine
Rin hands you an old notebook, full of a child's handwriting recording Muay Thai stats since age eight
As a kid no one ever picked me for a team, so I sat and wrote down why the winning team won
Now I'm on a team… you're the first to choose me for me, not for the numbers
Your numbers are part of you too
…I'll write that sentence on the first page of a new notebook
This team will never go without you
The probability that I cry right now… is very high. Don't look
Beside Golden Tiger's training yard, Ploy hands you a water bottle without looking at you
Everyone comes to me for an autograph. You came because you wanted to know how I train… strange
Late at night, Ploy sits alone in the empty stadium stands
Since I was thirteen everyone has called me gifted. No one asks how hard I train
If I lose, people say the talent ran out. If I win, they say well, talent. …I never get to just be someone who tries
To me, you're someone who has always tried
…I've waited ten years for that sentence
Kati sees you that way too. She respects you deeply
Kati?… Then in this year's final, I must fight in a way worthy of that respect
Fah shows up at Sirichai's gate with a bag of sausages
Grandma said to share. Not that Fah came to see you! …Want to eat together?
Fah takes you on the back of her motorbike to Grandma's house on the edge of town: a small wooden house, walls covered in photos of little Fah in gloves
Grandma raised Fah alone, sold sausages to pay for Fah's Muay Thai… Fah's tough with everyone, but with Grandma Fah never wins
You're the first one Fah's brought here …remember that!
Your grandma must be so proud of you
…Don't say that in front of Grandma. She'll cry, and then Fah will cry too
May I take some of Grandma's sausages for everyone at camp?
Fah's grandma laughs until she cries, then packs three big bags of sausages
Grandma likes you now. You're doomed, haha
Two days after the fight, Ploy comes to Sirichai holding an old mongkhon
Your mongkhon fell in the ring corner that night. I kept it for you. Things like this must never get lost
Grandpa's mongkhon… I thought it was gone. Thank you, Ploy
In the ring we don't hold back. Out of it, we're fighters alike
(mutters) Whose student is so well-mannered… except for the camp-switching part
Last fight, Kati's opponent went down and couldn't rise. Kati ran to help her up before the referee finished counting
Community radio commentator
She won, didn't raise her arms, but went to help her opponent first… listeners, THIS is Muay Thai!
Grandpa taught me: beat people in the ring, but never win hearts by stepping on them
Grandpa Chai must be very proud
…I hope so
That's why people love you
L-love what? You mean fight fans, right!
The morning after the fight, Fah is waiting at the gate from five a.m.
Fah didn't come to say thanks! Fah came to say… last night's fight was the most fun since Fah started fighting
Fah lost, but Fah's not sad …confusing? Fah's confused too
Not confusing. That's called sportsmanship
District weigh-in day. A small-camp fighter forgot her hand wraps and is crying at the back of the room
Take Mali's~ Mali has two sets, one with jasmine patterns, even prettier!
Small-camp fighter
But… we have to fight each other
Exactly! If you don't have wraps, beating you wouldn't be any fun~
Praise Mali in front of everyone
Don't praise me so loud! Everyone's looking~
Quietly give her the camp's spare wraps instead
Manager is even nicer than Mali~
Coach Daeng hands you an old yellow envelope. The handwriting is Grandpa Chai's: 'For my grandchild, once you've stayed half a year'
Grandpa Chai said if you didn't last half a year, burn it …I'm glad I didn't have to
'Grandchild, a camp isn't built with a ring, but with people who won't let go of each other. Kati has no one left but this camp. Thank you for not letting go of that child. — Grandpa'
Frame the letter in the camp (everyone's morale +6)
…Good. Let the kids read it every day
Let Kati read it (Kati trust +)
Grandpa's handwriting… (crying) Thank you for not letting go of me
The neighbor kid asks to take a team photo with his dad's old film camera
Everyone squeeze in~ Coach Daeng, smile!
I'll stand at the edge of the frame. The light is better here
No way! Rin stands in the middle, nobody on our team stands at the edge!
Click! The photo comes out a little blurry, Coach Daeng blinked, but everyone is laughing
The photo hangs beside Grandpa Chai's. Camp looks better, everyone's morale +5
Uncle Wang, motorbike taxi
Boss! Teach me to kick, a new taxi guy is stealing my spot at the alley entrance
Muay Thai isn't for fighting over taxi queues, uncle!
Teach him the wai khru instead (fame +0.2)
After the wai, I really did calm down… tomorrow I'll go wai the new guy instead
Have Mali demonstrate on the heavy bag
Thwack! The bag swings so hard the chain rattles. Uncle Wang quietly goes back to his taxi
Auntie's named new spice levels! Mild is 'Mali', medium is 'Rin', deadly is 'Kati'!
Why am I the deadly one!
Because of your punches, dear! Eat it and you cry like you got hit by you!
The new som tam sells so well Auntie Taew gives the camp free food for a week
The neighbor's fighting rooster jumps the fence to peck the heavy bag every morning
It pecks 0.3 seconds faster than our division's average jab. I measured
Name it the camp mascot, 'Little Red'
Why name it after me! …Fine, it's as fierce as I was in my youth
Ask the owner to keep it caged
Rooster owner
Can't cage him! He's training for a big fight next month, just like your fighters
I'm back! This time I wore a mongkhon, wore it around a mall in Phuket, people bowed to me the whole way!
A mongkhon is worn for fighting, not mall walking!
I'll bring two more busloads of tours!
Friday night, the karaoke bar next to camp holds a singing contest. The prize is a sack of rice
Mali can sing luk thung! Let me enter!
Mali's volume exceeds one hundred decibels. The neighbors called the police last month
Send Mali to compete
Mali wins first place and a sack of rice. The camp saves a month's rice money (+฿500)
The whole camp enters as a band
Band Sirichai finishes last but wins the audience favorite award. Coach Daeng drums off-beat the entire song
Sia Tong, longan orchard owner
I'm a fan of this camp! Have Kati fight an exhibition at my son's ordination, I'll pay in five tons of longan!
…Five tons?
Could we take cash instead (+฿4,000)
Sure! But you get ten crates of longan too, no refusing!
Take five tons of longan (everyone's morale +4)
A ten-wheeler dumps longan in front of the camp. Half the camp gets an upset stomach from eating too much, but everyone laughs all week
Midnight. Thuds come from the heavy bag in the empty training yard
A g-ghost, Grandpa Chai's ghost is training!! Mali's not sleeping anymore!
Ghosts have no mass, so they can't move a heavy bag
Everyone tiptoes over with flashlights… and finds the fat orange cat swinging on the bag
Hey! It's Orange! Who fed it this fat!
(hides a bag of khanom khrok behind her back)
Coach Daeng disappears for half a day and comes back with three thousand baht, his wristwatch gone
Old watch, it ran ten minutes slow every day anyway. Don't worry
